blocks.text: Respiratory pigments are special proteins in the blood or tissues that transport oxygen throughout the body. They also serve other purposes, such as storing O2, transporting CO2 and transporting substances other than respiratory gases. The two well-known respiratory pigments are haemoglobin and myoglobin.

Haemoglobin is a protein present in the RBCs. A haemoglobin molecule is composed of four globin (globular) polypeptide chains, two alpha and two beta, and four haem groups. The alpha chain has 141 amino acids and the beta chain 146. Each polypeptide chain is folded so that it contains a pocket where a haem group binds, so each chain is associated with one haem group. A haem group consists of an iron ion held in a porphyrin ring; the iron ion is attached to four nitrogen atoms of the polypeptide chain. Under a higher partial pressure of oxygen the iron ion attaches a molecule of O2, so one haemoglobin molecule can carry up to four O2 molecules.

blocks.title: Holding the four chains together
blocks.text: The four polypeptide chains of haemoglobin are bound to each other by salt bridges, hydrogen bonds and the hydrophobic effect.

Myoglobin is the oxygen-binding protein in the skeletal and cardiac muscle cells of vertebrates, and gives muscle its distinct red or dark grey colour. It is a monomer composed of a single polypeptide chain of 153 amino acids with a single haem group, so it binds a single O2 molecule. Its binding affinity is high compared with that of haemoglobin, so myoglobin serves as the oxygen-storing protein in muscles: it releases oxygen only when the partial pressure of oxygen falls below 20 mm Hg, and in this way provides oxygen to the muscles when they need it.

blocks.long_description: Haemoglobin has four globin chains, two alpha of 141 amino acids and two beta of 146, held together by salt bridges, hydrogen bonds and the hydrophobic effect; each chain folds into a pocket holding a haem group, an iron ion in a porphyrin ring, and each iron binds one oxygen molecule at high partial pressure, so the molecule carries up to four. Myoglobin is one chain of 153 amino acids with one haem, so it binds one oxygen; it holds oxygen more tightly and releases it only below 20 mm Hg, storing it in skeletal and cardiac muscle.
